blocks.text: The report is built so that a Board member can read the summary and any one focus area on its own, and a programme owner can run the plan from Chapters 3 to 5.
The report moves from context to evidence to recommendations to delivery.

The executive summary tells the case in short: where the province stands, what caps growth and what 2.5 million arrivals would take. It then sets out the three shifts and the twenty focus areas, the first 24 months, the headline indicators and the main risks. It stands alone, for the Board, Exco and the February 2027 launch audience. Chapter 1 is for every reader, and is the chapter of the body a Board member should read if they read no other. It sets out what Wesgro asked for, where the system stands after recovery, why the next step is constrained by peak capacity and how the study ran.

Chapter 2 sets out what the analysis found, in four parts: the global benchmarks and their lessons, demand, supply and the enabling environment. It serves readers checking the evidence behind a Chapter 3 entry, and each part closes with a box naming the focus areas it supports. Chapter 3 takes the twenty focus areas in turn. Each entry sets out the challenge or opportunity, the evidence, the course of action, why it can work and the link to the plan. The Board and Exco can read it entry by entry and the programme owner in full; section 3.4 gives the sequence.

Chapter 4 sets out which initiatives run, in what order, owned by whom, at what cost and with which decision gates, for the programme owner, Steerco and the partners named in the RACI. Chapter 5 sets out how progress is measured, through indicators, baselines, targets, data sources, the scorecard and the 2030 mid-term review, for Wesgro Research, the programme office and Steerco. Appendices A1 to A9 hold the traceability table, the demand model, the benchmark cases, readiness scores, the community fact base, stakeholder inputs, charters, the toolkit and references, for analysts and anyone checking a figure.

Sources sit in footnotes, one per paragraph, in the order the paragraph uses them. Each study document is cited by a short title and page, in the form Demand-Side Analysis, p21; Appendix A9 gives each full title and cover date. The executive summary carries no footnotes, because the chapters source its figures. The page is the PDF page index counted from the cover, because none of the decks prints page numbers. The MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment and the three Skift memos have no fixed pagination and are cited by section title.
Where a deliverable's file carries a later date than its cover, Appendix A9 shows both.

Where two inputs disagree the report states the value it uses, names the other with its page and gives the reason. The five-market share, printed as both 63% and 61% on one slide, is one case (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p13). Nothing is averaged and nothing is reconciled silently.
Section 1.1 sets out how the report counts arrivals; the 2.5 million goal is the accelerated case rounded.

Highlighted text in square brackets marks an open item: a figure no input in hand carries, with the figure needed and who holds it. Every page of this draft carries DRAFT FOR DISCUSSION in its header and the cover carries a draft line; both come off at sign-off.

Three codes tie the chapters together. A Chapter 3 kicker names the entry's theme, 1.1 to 3.2, above the focus area name as it reads on the tree [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026, pp15 to 16: deck page reference to be confirmed]; each entry closes with the initiative and indicator it links to. Initiatives in Chapter 4 run I1 onwards in one sequence; indicators in Chapter 5 run T1-01 onwards for impact, T2-01 for outcome and T3-01 for output.

Appendix A1 holds the evidence behind the tree. For each focus area it records the workstream and Chapter 2 sections behind it, rates the strength of the evidence and gives its initiative and indicator codes. Any Chapter 3 claim can be followed back to a page and forward to an owner and a measure. Nine focus areas rest on strong evidence and ten on adequate evidence. Two of the ten rest on indirect evidence: focus area 5 has no fare or yield data, and focus area 15 is an inference from the pipeline tables. Focus area 20 waits on a labour analysis still to be commissioned.
